script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for October 15, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

sentences: Story 1 is about Isoflurane-Based Inhaled Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adults With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: The SAVE-ICU Randomized Clinical Trial..
This is a randomized / clinical trial from JAMA.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in intensive care units (ICUs) in Canada, how should we interpret oxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is limited. To evaluate whether an inhaled sedation strategy lowers hospital mortality compared with usual care intravenous sedation strategy in mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF. Pragmatic, effectiveness, open-lab?

Of 786 patients randomized, 780 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 61.1 years; 34.0% female; 73.7% non-COVID AHRF, mean Pao2:Fio2 ratio, 152.6 mm Hg); 385 in the inhaled sedation and 395 in the intravenous sedation groups.
In the inhaled sedation group, 49.9% to 55.4% of patients received concomitant intravenous sedation on any day during the first 14 days after randomization.

articles.title: Isoflurane-Based Inhaled Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adults With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: The SAVE-ICU Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: Adults (≥18 years) receiving sedation for less than 72 hours and receiving mechanical ventilation for AHRF from non-COVID respiratory failure (ratio of partial pressure of arterial oxygen [Pao2] to fraction of inspired oxygen [Fio2] <300 mm Hg) or COVID-19 were enrolled between September 2020 and March 2025 with follow-up through June 2025. Patients were randomized to an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed or to a usual intravenous sedation care strategy. Sedatives were titrated to achieve the desired target sedation score guided by clinical teams and continued until extubation or death. Of 786 patients randomized, 780 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 61.1 years; 34.0% female; 73.7% non-COVID AHRF, mean Pao2:Fio2 ratio, 152.6 mm Hg); 385 in the inhaled sedation and 395 in the intravenous sedation groups. In the inhaled sedation group, 49.9% to 55.4% of patients received concomitant intravenous sedation on any day during the first 14 days after randomization.

The inhaled sedation group received more adjunctive therapies for hypoxemia (239 [63.9%] vs 214 [55.0%]; between-group difference, 8.89% [95% CI, 1.95% to 15.83%]) and had fewer delirium- and coma-free days (between-group difference, -0.95 [95% CI, -1.69 to -0.22]).

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
articles.summary: Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%).

articles.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine.
